findings.title: Workflow pre-existing-path guard is non-enforcing and can upload rejected pre-existing public bytes
findings.evidence: The CPU shell uses `set -uo pipefail`, without `-e`. The standalone `test ! -e private && test ! -e stage && test ! -e public` result is neither checked nor followed by exit, so a pre-existing path does not stop execution. cpu_publish correctly rejects a pre-existing public output, but the artifact step is `if: always()` and uploads that same path. A pre-existing public directory can therefore survive publisher rejection and still be uploaded. Existing tests exercise the Python publisher's conflict rejection and only string-match the workflow; they do not execute the shell plus always-upload behavior.
findings.privacyImpact: Potential publication of bytes that were never exact-one validated or produced by cpu_publish.
findings.minimumCorrection: Give the CPU step an id; explicitly exit on any pre-existing private/stage/public path; emit a publication-ready output only after cpu_publish returns zero; gate the always artifact step on that output while retaining if-no-files-found:error. This still permits upload of a bounded failure/fallback after the final CPU status test fails, but skips upload whenever publication itself or the precondition fails. Add a workflow-level shell model covering pre-existing private, stage, and public paths.

independentCpuReplay.limitation: The suite does not execute the workflow shell and artifact-step condition, so it does not cover R1.
